lines.en: Hi Omar! I cannot believe this is our last day of level B2.
I know. It feels like we only started yesterday.
Do you remember our first discussion about opinions?
I would rather hear an honest disagreement than a polite agreement that hides the truth.
However strong his opinion may be, he should still listen to those who disagree with him.
What really matters is not who wins the argument, but whether we get closer to the truth.
Not only did she defend her position calmly, but she also managed to change several minds in the room.
Speaking of strong opinions, do you still argue with your uncle about success and luck?
Success is rarely the result of luck; more often, it is the reward for refusing to give up.
It was not talent that made her successful, but years of disciplined practice.
Failing once does not make you a failure, just as succeeding once does not make you a master.
My uncle would say the city makes people fight harder for success.
Living downtown may be convenient, but it comes at the cost of peace and quiet.
What I miss most about village life is the silence you can never find in a crowded city.
If the government were to invest more in public transport, traffic would not be such a daily struggle.
Under no circumstances should historic buildings be demolished to make room for parking lots.
Did you read about the new study on the human brain?
The discovery is said to have changed the way scientists understand the human brain.
It is widely believed that water once flowed on the surface of Mars.
Little did the scientists expect that their small project would lead to a Nobel Prize.
If it were not for vaccines, millions of lives would have been lost to diseases we now rarely see.
You always loved science. I was the one painting in the corner.
What draws people to art is not its price, but the feelings it awakens in them.
However difficult the first attempts may seem, every artist was once a beginner.
Not only does music express what words cannot, but it also connects people across cultures.
What matters in art is not perfection, but honesty; a painting must say something true.
Maybe your art could become a business one day.
What separates a successful startup from a failing one is rarely the idea itself, but the way it is carried out.
What investors really look for is not a perfect plan, but a team they can trust.
However brilliant your product is, nobody will buy it if they have never heard of it.
It was her ability to adapt, not her original idea, that saved the business during the crisis.
A business needs customers, and customers come from media and advertising.
It is no exaggeration to say that advertising shapes what we want without us noticing.
What makes an advertisement memorable is rarely its budget, but the story it tells.
Not only do advertisers sell products, but they also sell dreams and lifestyles.
What we should teach children is not to avoid media, but to question it.
Advertising has rules too. That is where law comes in.
It is a basic principle that everyone is innocent until proven guilty.
However strict the law may be, it means little if it is not applied equally to everyone.
What the victim wanted was not revenge, but simply to be heard.
What makes a society just is not the number of its laws, but the fairness with which they are applied.
Law is about behavior, and so is psychology. Did you finish that book?
The more we understand our own fears, the less power they have over us.
However confident someone appears, they may be fighting battles nobody knows about.
It is said that we make most of our decisions emotionally and then justify them with logic.
Rarely do we realize how much our childhood shapes the adults we become.
You know what builds confidence too? Sports.
What separates champions from ordinary players is not talent alone, but the will to train when nobody is watching.
Not until the final minute did the team score the goal that made them champions.
What the fans remember is not the score, but the moment the whole stadium stood up.
Losing a final is painful, but it teaches a team lessons that victory never could.
The whole country watched that final together, like one family.
Not until every country works together will we solve problems that cross all borders.
What makes climate change so dangerous is that its worst effects will be felt by those who caused it least.
It is often the poorest communities that pay the highest price for decisions made far away.
Rarely has the world needed cooperation as urgently as it does today.
Cooperation built this country too. Think of our history.
What amazes visitors is not only the size of the temples, but the precision with which they were built.
It is believed that the pyramids were built by paid workers rather than slaves.
It was the discovery of the Rosetta Stone that opened the door to understanding hieroglyphs.
Were these monuments to be destroyed, no money in the world could ever rebuild them.
And today, we build new things on top of that history.
It is often a simple frustration that leads to the most useful inventions.
Not only did the printing press spread knowledge, but it also changed who was allowed to have it.
However advanced an invention may be, it is useless unless people can actually afford it.
What drives most inventors is not money, but the joy of solving a problem nobody else could solve.
All these inventions are supposed to bring people together, but do they?
What modern life has taken from us is the time to simply sit with one another and talk.
What holds a family together is not the absence of conflict, but the willingness to forgive.
However busy life becomes, we should never be too busy for the people we love.
Being close to people is a kind of safety too, I think.
It is impossible to remove all risk from life; the best we can do is to manage it wisely.
It is often the risks we ignore, not the ones we fear, that end up hurting us.
Rarely does fear protect us as well as preparation does.
Were everyone to follow the safety instructions, most accidents would never happen.
Speaking of safety, my laptop broke again. Time for another complaint letter.
I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the service I received at your branch last week.
What I find particularly disappointing is that nobody has replied to my previous three emails.
However polite a complaint letter may be, it should still state clearly what action is expected.
It was not until I threatened to contact consumer protection that the company finally responded.
And after the letter comes the negotiation.
What every skilled negotiator knows is that listening is more powerful than speaking.
Not until both sides feel they have gained something is a deal truly successful.
However tempting it may be to win every point, a good negotiator knows when to compromise.
It is rarely the loudest voice in the room that wins the negotiation.
After all this city noise, I dream of the desert again.
What makes the desert so remarkable is the variety of life that survives in such harsh conditions.
Not until the reserve was established did the number of gazelles begin to recover.
It is not the strongest species that survives, but the one most able to adapt.
What conservation needs most is not more money, but more people who genuinely care.
Protecting nature also costs money, which brings us to the economy.
What worries economists is not the debt itself, but the speed at which it is growing.
The price of bread is said to affect political stability more than any election speech.
It is not wealth that makes a country stable, but the fairness with which that wealth is shared.
Rarely do economists agree on anything, yet they all warn against ignoring inflation.
Money questions are hard, but moral questions are harder.
What makes a dilemma a dilemma is that every choice carries a cost someone must pay.
It is not always easy to know where honesty ends and cruelty begins.
It is said that character is what you do when nobody is watching.
Rarely is the easiest choice also the right one.
When life feels heavy, I look up at the stars.
It is believed that the universe contains more stars than there are grains of sand on all our beaches.
Not until the telescope was invented did we understand that Earth is not the center of everything.
What a night in the desert teaches you is that the sky is not a ceiling, but a window.
And look how we are talking about all of this, in a new language.
What makes language such a powerful tool is that it can carry an idea from one mind to another.
Not until a language loses its last speaker does it truly die.
It is not the words themselves, but the tone and the silence between them, that carry the real meaning.
What children teach us about language is that rules are learned by listening, not by studying.
Learning English changed us, did it not?
However painful a change may be at first, it often opens doors we never knew existed.
It is not the change itself that frightens people, but the fear of losing what they know.
What survivors of any crisis share is not strength, but the willingness to adapt.
Rarely does life ask our permission before it changes; it simply changes, and we must follow.
Any regrets about the journey, Omar?
What most people regret is not the mistakes they made, but the chances they never took.
If only we had known how quickly time passes, we would have spent more evenings together.
I would rather fail at something I love than succeed at something that means nothing to me.
Rarely do we get second chances, so it is wiser to treat the first one with care.
So, what is next for us after B2?
Level C1 is waiting for us. Are you ready?
Ready. We argued, we learned, and we never gave up.
And this time, no complaining about a single lesson.
I do not promise that, but I promise to finish. See you in C1, Sara!
See you there, Omar. It was a wonderful journey.
